audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's phases[].side chart and the content layer's win[] chart disagreed on all seven rows (full read Karma,Karma,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill; content and packet read Skill,Skill,Karma,Karma,Ekko,Ekko,Ekko).
audit.why: Packet levelChart and content win[] agree with each other and with the kit: Karma's Mantra is available from level 1 with no skill point, so her empowered Inner Flame plus a flat-12s Focused Resolve root peaks at 3-5, while Ekko's Chronobreak (110/80/50) and item scaling take over from 6.
audit.corrected: phases[].side set to Skill, Skill, Karma, Karma, Ekko, Ekko, Ekko with the whys rewritten to match; content win[] already holds those exact values so no win[] edit was possible.
sources: enemyKit R text: 'Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point'

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] claimed Mantra-empowered Soulflare 'becomes available around level 3-5'; spikes[1] called Focused Resolve a 'long-range root chain'.
audit.why: Mantra requires no skill point and exists from level 1; Focused Resolve is 675 range, shorter than Ekko's 1075 Q.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] now states Mantra is up from level 1 on a 40/38/36/34s cooldown shortened by every damaging spell; spikes[1] names the 675-range tether and Chronobreak's untargetable rewind.
sources: enemyKit Q/W/R cooldowns, ranges and text

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1], wants.foe[0] and wants.foe[1] attributed the root to Mantra-Q and the shield/move speed to W.
audit.why: Per the kit, the root is Focused Resolve (W, flat 12s, also reveals stealth; Mantra extends the root and heals Karma) and the shield plus move speed is Inspire (E, 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, Mantra spreads it to nearby allies). Karma's Mantra-Q cataclysm damages after a delay, it does not root.
audit.corrected: Root reassigned to Focused Resolve, shield/speed to Inspire, and the Mantra-W self-heal called out as the reason Grievous Wounds matters in long fights (from _missing: needs-antiheal).
sources: brief enemyKit W and E text/flags

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT); dosFull[2].d called it a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is a flat 12 seconds at every rank; Mantra is 40/38/36/34s; Chronobreak is 110/80/50s.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and the twelve-second window corrected in dosFull[2].d.
sources: brief enemyKit W cd '12', R cd '40/38/36/34'

audit.corrected: All flagged pronouns corrected and the three bled bullets replaced with bodies that match their titles.

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Q the wave and her toes — the return pass chunks, and your 1075 range beats Inner Flame's 950 on the poke.

edits.before: W zone games begin: drop it on his retreat line BEFORE trading and the stun finds him mid-regret.
edits.after: Her Mantra window bites: Focused Resolve roots on a flat 12s — pre-place W on her line, go only after it.

edits.before: Three-hit trades on cooldown — Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk. Bank the tempo for 6.
edits.after: Inner Flame hits 6s at rank 4 and refunds Mantra — farm on Q passes and bank the tempo for 6.

edits.before: Level 3 favors Karma outright since her Mantra-Soulflare root-burn combo comes online and Ekko has no comparable answer at this level.
edits.after: Level 3 favors Karma: Focused Resolve on a flat 12s roots you out of Phase Dive range while her Mantra Inner Flame burns the ground you land on.

edits.before: Level 4 stays Karma-favored as she continues to abuse the Soulflare combo on cooldown to zone you off farm and chip your health.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay Karma-favored — Inner Flame drops to 6s at rank 4 and every cast shaves her Mantra cooldown, so the zoning never lapses.

edits.before: Level 5 flips to Ekko because your base kit's damage and mobility start catching up while Karma's combo cooldown can't keep pace with her lack of scaling.
edits.after: Level 6 flips to Ekko: Chronobreak rewinds you out of her Mantra burst on a 110s cooldown, and Parallel Convergence's stun turns a 12s tether whiff into a kill.

edits.before: Level 6 favors Ekko since Chronobreak gives you safety from her root chain and her ultimate offers no burst spike to counter your growing power.
edits.after: First item is Ekko's: the Q-E-passive string plus one item chunks half her bar, and Inspire's shield on an 8s cooldown cannot cover a full rotation.

edits.before: Karma's Mantra-empowered Soulflare (RQ) becomes available around level 3-5 giving her a big root-and-burn poke combo that punishes any greedy CS animation, this is her strongest poke window before Ekko has enough combat stats to trade back.
edits.after: Mantra needs no skill point and is up from level 1, so her empowered Inner Flame exists before your combo does; on a 40s Mantra shortened by every damaging spell, levels 3-5 are when she chains it often enough to zone you off the wave.

edits.before: Ekko's actual level 6 doesn't add a burst spike over Karma's mantra combo, but it does give you Chronobreak as an escape from her long-range root chain, and from here your base kit's damage starts to outpace her poke-only kit.
edits.after: Level 6 adds no burst over her Mantra combo, but Chronobreak's untargetable rewind pulls you out of Focused Resolve's 675-range tether before the root lands, and from here your base damage outpaces her poke-only kit.

edits.before: Once you finish a first item, Ekko's all-in via Phase Dive plus Z-Drive Resonance easily out-trades Karma's remaining mana-hungry poke, especially since she has no hard CC beyond the Soulflare root to punish your engage.
edits.after: With a first item, Phase Dive plus the Z-Drive Resonance third hit out-trades her mana-hungry poke — Inner Flame costs up to 80 and Inspire 80, so a Focused Resolve whiffed on 12s leaves her no CC to punish your engage.

edits.before: Levels 3-4 clearly favor Karma once Mantra unlocks Soulflare, since the root-into-burn combo punishes any CS attempt and she can zone you off half the wave without real retaliation; by level 6 the tide turns because Ekko's kit finally has enough base damage and Chronobreak safety to start pressuring back despite her having no true ultimate spike of her own.
edits.after: Levels 3-4 clearly favor Karma — Mantra needs no skill point and is up from level 1, so the empowered Inner Flame and the flat-12s Focused Resolve root punish any CS attempt and zone you off half the wave; by level 6 the tide turns, because Chronobreak's untargetable rewind erases her best combo and your base damage finally outpaces a kit with no burst ultimate.
